findings.title: Retry-count cleanup deletes workflow reminders too broadly
findings.body: The deleteMany OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` is not scoped to SMS reminders or to unscheduled reminders. As written, any WorkflowReminder row (including EMAIL or WHATSAPP reminders, or a reminder that is already scheduled) will be deleted if its retryCount is greater than 1. This can delete data outside the intended SMS retry flow; the condition should include at least `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and likely `scheduled: false`.

findings.title: Retry count is incremented from a stale read instead of atomically
findings.body: Both failure paths set `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read before the SMS attempt. If two executions of this endpoint process the same reminder concurrently, the absolute writes can overwrite each other and the reminder may not reach the deletion threshold as intended. Use Prisma's atomic update, e.g. `retryCount: { increment: 1 }`, including in the catch block at line 195.

findings.title: Reminders with an empty message or missing recipient never count as failed
findings.body: The retry count is only incremented when `message?.length > 0 && sendTo` is true and scheduling fails. If `sendTo` is missing or the rendered message is empty, the reminder is skipped without incrementing `retryCount`, so it will be re-selected on every cron run until `scheduledDate` passes instead of being cleaned up by the new retry logic. These cases should either increment retryCount or be explicitly deleted/cancelled.

findings.title: No tests cover the new retry/deletion behavior
findings.body: The PR introduces destructive cleanup based on retryCount but no tests verify that failed SMS attempts increment the counter, that reminders are deleted only after the intended number of failures, and that the deletion query is correctly scoped. Without coverage, regressions in this background job could silently drop workflow reminders.
